benchmark: The average industry: every NSE industry or sector group with a reading that day, each weighted equally. Each group is itself the equal-weighted average of its counted stocks.

market.note: The Nifty 50 is below its 200-day exponential average. In the study, industry thrusts in such markets were followed by stronger industry returns than usual (from a small number of separate episodes).

corner_meanings.Ahead and gaining: Ahead of the average industry over 6 months, and still gaining ground last month
corner_meanings.Ahead but slowing: Ahead over 6 months, but behind the average last month
corner_meanings.Behind and slipping: Behind the average industry over 6 months, and still losing ground last month
corner_meanings.Behind but gaining: Behind over 6 months, but ahead of the average last month

method.benchmark: The average industry: every NSE industry or sector group with a reading that day, each weighted equally. Each group is itself the equal-weighted average of its counted stocks.
method.strength: 6-month return of the group minus the average industry's, in points.
method.change: Last month's return of the group minus the average industry's, in points.
method.corner: Strength above 0 is ahead, otherwise behind. Change above 0 is gaining, otherwise slowing (when ahead) or slipping (when behind). A group moves to a new corner only after two weekly closes in it.
method.breadth: Share of the group's counted stocks above their 50-day average: 50% or more is broad, under 40% narrow.
method.rank: A 0-100 score: the 3, 6 and 12-month returns against the average industry, ranked across groups and weighted 0.3, 0.4 and 0.3, make up three quarters; the breadth reading, ranked the same way, makes up the last quarter. Rank 1 has the highest score. Changes compare with the previous weekly close.
method.week: Weekly readings use each week's last session. The current week uses its latest session until it closes.

text.ahead_gaining: 4,902 cases: over the next 3 months these groups did +1.2 points against the average industry, and 54% beat it. With broad breadth +1.4; with narrow breadth +0.4.
text.ahead_slowing: 2,847 cases: +0.7 points over the next 3 months (50% beat the average). 66% of moves out of this corner went back to Ahead and gaining.
text.behind_slipping: 5,766 cases: -1.1 points over the next 3 months; 40% beat the average industry.
text.behind_gaining: 2,713 cases: +0.4 points over the next 3 months (49% beat the average). Only 26% of moves out of this corner led to Ahead and gaining; 72% went back to Behind and slipping. It has usually been a bounce, not the start of a lead.
text.spread: Groups Ahead and gaining did 2.3 points better over the next 3 months than groups Behind and slipping, averaged week by week. The gap was 2.6 points when the Nifty 50 was above its 200-day average and 1.1 when it was below.
text.rank: The top third by rotation rank did 2.8 points better over the next 3 months than the bottom third, in 72% of weeks. Groups that climbed 5 or more places in 4 weeks did +1.0 points over the next 3 months; groups that fell 5 or more did -0.7.
text.stay: A group stayed a median of 5 weeks in a corner (mean 7.2).
limits: Groups often move together in the same weeks, so the cases are not independent; averages are taken week by week.

The same rules on 18 of NSE's own sector indices, which are weighted by company size, against the Nifty 500: +0.4 points over 3 months, with no reliable pattern year to year. The pattern lives in how the typical stock of an industry moves.
The rules (6 months, 1 month, two weekly closes, the rank weights) were chosen after testing a few versions on this same data, so expect live results to be weaker.
Each company's NSE industry is today's label, even for earlier years.
Returns ignore costs and taxes; the groups are equal-weighted, so they lean towards mid and small companies.
